summary: Advertising page from a Victorian broadsheet: railroad timetables, sewing machines, liquor and patent medicine. No liners at all; every ad is a centred stack of mixed display faces, many with an engraved cut.

frame.masthead: Running head across the top: paper name, weekday, date in caps.

headers.notes: Small caps with a full stop, centred between hairlines. Acts as a category label but sits above a single advertiser.

units.example: THE HOWE SEWING MACHINE / The Grandest Production of Inventive Genius
units.notes: Each line a different face and size: woodtype name, italic tagline, spaced caps. Medallion engraving at top.

units.example: 1871. SUMMER TIME TABLE. 1871. / Leave St. Paul ... 7.30 a.m.
units.notes: Locomotive cut above a two-column table with dot leaders. Spans the widest column.
White shaded letters out of a black engraved block, an early reverse-out.

type.look: Heavy fat-face and Clarendon woodtype, some outlined or shaded
Bold Clarendon caps for advertiser names
Small Scotch Roman / modern serif, tightly set

notes: Column widths vary to fit each ad, not a fixed grid.
The small insertion codes at the bottom right of ads (m18 1m) would add realism to a generator.
